hook.text: Gamblers blow on dice before rolling. They're not changing physics. But it feels like they're in charge.

buildup.text: The illusion of control: believing you influence outcomes that are actually random or beyond your power.

discovery.text: Ellen Langer found people value self-chosen lottery tickets more than assigned ones—same odds, more confidence.

twist.text: Traders fall for this too. Active stock-picking often underperforms index funds, but it feels more controlled.

climax.text: The illusion is comforting. Accepting randomness means accepting deep vulnerability, and brains resist that.

punchline.text: Feeling in control isn't being in control.

quiz.question: What is the illusion of control?
